fr.recommendations: Based on the observed site characteristics, personnel responding to this property would benefit from pre-identifying all available access points along the street frontage, as multiple entry options could facilitate more effective positioning and staging of apparatus. Vehicle congestion within the parking areas and drive aisle may affect apparatus maneuvering and should be anticipated when planning approach routes. Limited access along the rear of the property could affect movement and positioning for operations in that area, making early awareness of this constraint valuable. Dense vegetation within the landscaped areas may reduce visibility and could affect navigation around the structure, particularly near pedestrian walkways and the front entry area.

wildfire.recommendations: Managing the tree cluster and scattered trees across the property by increasing horizontal spacing between individual trees and woody shrubs could reduce fuel continuity and limit the opportunity for fire to move through the canopy layer. Reducing direct vegetation contact along the structure perimeter, particularly where shrubs and mixed vegetation cover are observed adjacent to the building, may reduce structure exposure and improve the immediate defensible space zone. Maintaining and expanding the existing open fuel break and irrigated landscape areas would support suppression operations and help sustain long-term fuel separation across the property. Given the single access route and limited rear access, keeping the primary driveway clear of encroaching vegetation and maintaining adequate vertical clearance along its full length would support firefighter access and allow for safer ingress and egress during an incident. Periodic monitoring of vegetation regrowth near the structure and along access corridors could support continued wildfire resilience over time.
